narrative.overview: PARADA is a zone-based campus parking system with two surfaces that deliberately do not share a palette: a driver app built around its own canonical mascot (a gate-attendant dog in navy with a gold badge) and an operations console built around the PARADA wordmark's own black-ink-and-orange-cut geometry. The driver app is warm-navy, badge-gold, azure and barrier-red because a driver meets PARADA through its mascot, outdoors, one-handed. The admin is true-neutral graphite lit by one restrained orange accent because an operator meets PARADA through the logo, at a desk, for hours, wanting instant status legibility. Consistency comes from typography, the cut-corner geometry, interaction quality and domain language, not from hex codes.
keyCharacteristics: Mobile: deep navy grounds, badge-gold brand accent, azure for active state, barrier-red for danger, signal-green for available.
Admin: true-neutral graphite grounds, logo-orange brand accent.
Shared typography (Space Grotesk / Inter / JetBrains Mono) and shared PARADA-cut geometry across both surfaces.
The canonical mascot is a fixed, unmodified image asset, mobile-only, used selectively.
Both themes (System/Light/Dark) are independently tuned per surface; light is never a literal inversion of dark.

rules.name: The Two-Palette Rule
rules.body: Mobile and admin never share a literal hex for their primary brand accent, even while sharing status semantics.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: A status is never color alone: every pill, badge and alert row carries an icon or dot plus a label.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on identifiers and machine values, never on labels, headings, or prose.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change sets in tabular numerals; admin's dashboard hero figures additionally settle via a short digit tween.

rules.name: The Panel-Level Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the outermost surface casts a shadow or frost; nested rows, chips and pills never do.

dos: Do keep mobile and admin's brand-accent hue distinct even while sharing status semantics.
Do draw the PARADA cut on every card/panel/button/input on both surfaces.
Do pair every status with an icon or label, never color alone.
Do compute any summary language from real query data; never fabricate availability or slot-level state.
Do use the canonical mascot image unmodified, only at empty/error/onboarding/greeting/confirmation moments.
Do animate live operational numbers with a settle/tween, gated behind Reduce Motion.
donts: Don't default a selector to a generic wrapping vertical card grid.
Don't let the mascot appear behind content or compete with the primary selector.
Don't invert light mode from dark mode on either surface.
Don't reuse Calamansi UI's own signature geometry or Persuade-mode effects in PARADA's Operate-mode admin.
Don't add a second filled accent-colored button to the same form or screen.
